headline: High-risk shared-state orchestration can leak or corrupt data; prompt-injection risk is lower but still present via shared graph outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can pass node outputs through shared graph state and supports multiple instances via a checkpointer store; mem0 is a knowledge-management component that may consume stored outputs. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if untrusted content is written into shared state. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF untrusted text is written into shared graph state and later re-read as instructions
IF mem0 stores or replays agent outputs without provenance labels
mitigations: Tag all stored content as data vs instructions before reuse.
Add a one-line sanitizer that strips tool directives from retrieved memory.
Disable automatic re-ingestion of raw agent outputs.
Review one sample memory record for prompt-like content.
requires-engineering: enforce provenance-aware retrieval in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph explicitly handles model-provider API keys and broad filesystem/network surfaces, while mem0 is a memory layer that can persist application state. If the shared graph state contains sensitive data, mem0 can retain it and LangGraph can route it through developer-defined tools. The pairwise leakage path exists in default orchestration patterns, though not all details are documented.
conditions: IF sensitive data is placed into graph state
IF mem0 persists that state without redaction
mitigations: Remove secrets from graph state before persistence.
Store only hashed or truncated identifiers in memory.
Audit one memory record for secrets or PII.
Turn off persistence for sensitive workflows.
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction before checkpointing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph has write_filesystem and broad network egress, and its shared checkpointer enables multiple instances; mem0 is a memory system that may also mutate shared application state. Even without explicit git/OAuth overlap, concurrent writes to the same logical state can conflict and overwrite each other. Because locking is not documented, uncertainty favors medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same checkpoint or memory namespace
IF no external lock serializes updates
mitigations: Assign separate namespaces per agent.
Add a manual lock around shared writes.
Check one recent conflict or overwrite in logs.
Reduce write frequency for one agent.
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency with version checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is an orchestration layer that can feed outputs from one node into another, and mem0 is designed to store and replay memory. If LangGraph treats retrieved memory as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into later actions. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF LangGraph routes mem0 retrievals directly into downstream action nodes
IF no verification step checks retrieved facts before use
mitigations: Insert a verification node before any action.
Require citations for retrieved facts.
Manually inspect one retrieved memory item.
Limit memory use to suggestions, not facts.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating on memory-derived outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either profile, and mem0 exposes no data classes while LangGraph mainly touches application-defined graph state. The only concrete compliance-relevant item is LangGraph handling model-provider API keys, which is not itself a residency breach. Because the evidence is sparse, keep this low rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared graph state
IF mem0 retention differs from the application's deletion policy
mitigations: Confirm what data classes enter the graph state.
Set a short retention window for memory.
Delete one test record and verify removal.
Avoid storing regulated data in mem0.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
